observable_outcome: One verified local commit becomes one branch a person can open on the real forge, published through the external side-effect protocol rather than through a bare command. An application command creates the Operation Intent and the Outbox Item in one domain transaction; the first production EffectSink in this repository delivers it; a content-addressed read-after-write confirms it: the blob object names the forge returns equal the local ones, the created tree object name equals the locally verified head tree, and the created ref's commit carries that same tree and exactly the base commit as its parent. The target comes only from a registered Repository reached through the Requirement's repository link, never from a caller-supplied coordinate. The write is a create-only ref under the reserved prefix agentic-loop/, never an update and never forced, and the string force appears as a key in no request body. An undecidable outcome reaches needs-input rather than a guess. No credential value enters argv, the environment or any file; the forge CLI reads its own store with an empty granted set; no raw forge response and no child standard error is recorded anywhere. git push is never attempted and no push argv is constructible: internal/runner/git.go, sourcecontrol.go, forge.go, confinement.go, supervisor.go and workspace.go are byte-identical, the git subcommand allowlist still has exactly fourteen entries, and the git child still receives no HOME. A confirmed publication changes no Requirement and no Increment status. make check reaches no network and starts no forge CLI child; exactly one gated live publication reaches the owner-designated repository, measures zero workflow runs on the branch, and records the ref and the commit so the branch can be found and deleted. The untouchable domain files, contracts/**, ci/**, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum, devbox.*, firestore.indexes.json, internal/api/**, internal/web/** and cmd/** are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: A1. Fixed implementation order with mid-task stops. Implement in this order and do not begin a leg before the previous one compiles and its tests pass: (1) internal/domain/repository.go, the two value objects and their validators; (2) internal/application/ports.go and internal/application/publication.go, the member interface and the publication command plus the target read and the observation write; (3) internal/application/service.go, the payload-carrying variant of effectOutbox; (4) internal/application/outbox.go, the single sentinel addition; (5) internal/store/memory; (6) internal/store/firestore; (7) internal/runner/publishsource.go, the payload derivation from a real commit; (8) internal/runner/forgepublish.go, the sink and the observer, with the injected in-process transport tests; (9) the protocol test through the real dispatcher; (10) the gated live leg; (11) docs; (12) evidence. If legs 1 to 4 are not green before leg 7 begins, stop and escalate rather than carrying a broken seam forward. Report, per leg, the argv actually run and its verdict line.

A2. No push, and the proof that no push is constructible is re-asserted. Do not add push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential or worktree to the git subcommand allowlist, do not add any key to the two-key -c option allowlist, and do not run gh auth setup-git, gh auth token or gh auth git-credential. Add a regression test asserting the allowlist has exactly fourteen entries, naming all fourteen, and asserting that an argv for each of push, fetch, remote, config and worktree is refused before any process could exist. internal/runner/git.go, sourcecontrol.go, forge.go, confinement.go, supervisor.go and workspace.go must be byte-identical at the end; report git diff --stat for internal/runner to prove it.

A3. The forge write is the Git Data API through the forge CLI, in a new type in a new file. Add internal/runner/forgepublish.go with a type distinct from ForgeClient. Do not add a write method to ForgeClient and do not edit internal/runner/forge.go: that file states in its own header that the adapter is read-only and has no code path that creates, modifies or deletes anything on the forge, and that statement must stay true. Reuse the same idiom by re-implementing it in the new type: resolve the executable through the shared resolveTool helper, refuse a non-absolute path, refuse a resolved path whose filepath.Base is not the expected tool name, refuse a path that stats to a directory, and refuse a non-empty granted set -- all before any process could exist, with an injectable stat hook so every refusal is deterministic and touches no filesystem.

A4. Guarded environment, empty grant set, credential nowhere. The forge child receives exactly the guarded base environment of HOME and PATH, built through the same construction internal/runner/forge.go uses and passed through GuardEnvironment and GuardCommand; the granted set must be empty and a non-empty one is refused. No credential value may appear in argv, in any environment entry, in any file this adapter writes, or in any error it returns. No new type in a non-test file may carry a field whose name contains token, secret, credential, password or auth, which internal/runner's existing source guard already checks and which must keep passing unmodified. Request bodies go to the child on standard input, never in argv.

A5. Four calls, each with its complete argv and body asserted. The adapter constructs exactly four write calls -- create blob, create tree, create commit, create ref -- and two read calls -- read ref, read commit -- plus one measurement read of the workflow-run count for the branch. Every argv states its method explicitly and names a repository path built from validated single-segment owner and name, so the argv itself witnesses what the call does. Assert every argv and every body field by field. Assert that no constructed body contains a key named force, over all four write bodies.

A6. The payload is derived from the verified commit, not from the ChangeSet. Add internal/runner/publishsource.go declaring a narrow second port and implementing it on GitSourceControl using only already-allowlisted subcommands: diff --name-only <base> <head> for the changed paths, ls-files --stage -- <path> for each path's mode and blob object name, and cat-file blob <object> for each path's bytes. Every such child runs confined exactly as V2-071's do, and each carries -C with the absolute working copy root. Content is sent to the forge base64-encoded so a binary file cannot corrupt a body. Assert against a real local commit that the derived modes and object names equal what the local repository reports for the same paths.

A7. Four refusals before any forge call. Refuse, with named sentinels and before any child starts: a ref that is not refs/heads/agentic-loop/ followed by a valid branch remainder; a staged mode that is not 100644 or 100755, naming symlink and gitlink modes as the cases this covers; a publication that would require deleting a path; and a publication whose changed-path count is zero. Assert each refusal, and assert that in each case no process was started.

A8. Create-only ref, never update, never force. The ref is created and never updated. There must be no code path that updates or forces a ref, and no argv or body naming an update method for a ref may be constructible. Prove it the way V2-071 proved push: the closed set of API operations this adapter can name is a list in one place, that list is read from exactly one place, and the list itself is what refuses anything else. Assert the refusal for a ref update and a ref delete as positive controls.

A9. Read-after-write is four content-addressed equalities. Confirmation requires all four: each blob object name the forge returned equals the local object name from ls-files --stage; the created tree object name equals the locally verified head tree from IntegrityObservation.TreeName; the ref's commit's tree object name equals that same local head tree; and that commit's parent list is exactly the one base commit. The ref name must equal the ref this operation intended. Assert each equality, and assert that a deliberate violation of each one individually is refused rather than confirmed. Record, and do not require, the comparison between the local commit object name and the published commit object name: they may legitimately differ because the forge constructs the commit object.

A10. Reads decide, error text never does. Parse no HTTP status code and no error body. Discard the child's standard error, bound its standard output with a hard byte cap, and return sentinels whose messages carry none of the child's bytes and none of a path outside the workspace. Duplicate detection is a read of the ref performed before the create, and a read of the ref performed again after any failure. Assert that no error returned by this adapter contains child output, by constructing failures on every path.

A11. Convergence, absence and disagreement are three measured outcomes. Ref absent then created and all equalities hold: confirm. Ref already present and its commit's tree equals the intended tree: converge as already successful, and assert that no second create call was made. Ref present and its commit's tree differs: undecidable, reaching needs-input. Assert all three, and assert that in the convergent case the operation identifier and the idempotency key were the same value as on the first attempt.

A12. One addition to internal/application/outbox.go and nothing else. Add one exported sentinel meaning the external outcome cannot be decided, and add one clause recognising it to the existing ambiguity predicate beside the deadline, cancellation and net.Error cases. Change no other line in that file, add no field to DispatcherConfig, and do not modify OutboxItem, the status vocabulary, claim, beforeEffect, deliver, ack, fail or resolveObservation. internal/application/outbox_test.go is a prohibited path: every existing outbox test must pass unmodified, and if any of them needs a change, STOP and escalate rather than editing it.

A13. The two records, in internal/domain/repository.go only. Add exactly two additive types beside the existing Repository, RepositoryObservation and RequirementRepositoryLink, with their own validate functions following the same precedent: a publication intent carrying repository identifier, locator, ref, base branch, base commit, head commit, head tree and changed-path count, which is serialised as the Outbox Item's Payload; and a publication Observation carrying operation identifier, repository identifier, ref, published commit, published tree, local commit, local tree, a tree-agreement flag, a closed state, a reason and observed_at. Store no URL on either record. Do not extend internal/domain/model.go's generic Validate or Decide type switches and do not add a field to Requirement, Increment, Execution, Lease, ControlIntent or Repository. internal/domain/model.go, control.go, lease.go, release.go and id.go must be byte-identical; report git diff --stat for internal/domain to prove it, and internal/domain/source_guard_test.go must keep passing unmodified.

A14. The Observation's state vocabulary is closed and cannot say completed. Declare the closed set of states the Observation may carry, with a terminal success value meaning published and observed. No value may mean completed, resolved, accepted or done, and an unobserved state must be a first-class value so that nothing measured is ever reported as a plausible-looking value that was never measured. Assert the closed set, including that an unknown value is refused.

A15. One member interface, one command, one target read, one observation write. Add to internal/application/ports.go exactly one interface -- carrying a write-once save of the publication Observation, a read by operation identifier, and a bounded read by increment identifier where a bool reports truncation -- and include it in UnitOfWork. Change no existing port method signature. Put the command, the target read and the observation write in a new file internal/application/publication.go. internal/application/repository.go and internal/application/readmodels.go are prohibited paths: do not add a view or a read model in this task.

A16. The command follows Capture's ceremony exactly and creates the Outbox Item in the same transaction. The publication command performs, in this order: the caller actor role check, requestedBy attribution, requireRequest on the request identifier, requestFingerprint for idempotency, s.mutate keyed by operation and request identifier, the idempotency read that replays a matching fingerprint and refuses a differing one, and then, inside the transaction, the target resolution of A17, then the existing effectOutbox path with the external-effect permit kind and a new outbox kind, then one s.record event. Add a payload parameter to effectOutbox and pass nil at its one existing call site so that call site's behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged; assert the existing accept-result outbox item is unchanged by testing it explicitly.

A17. The target can only be a registered Repository. Inside the same transaction, resolve owner and name only by reading the Execution, its Increment, that Increment's Requirement, the RequirementRepositoryLink for that Requirement, and the Repository that link names, taking the coordinate from the stored SourceLocator. There must be no field on the request and no environment variable in production through which a caller can name a coordinate. Refuse, creating no Outbox Item, when: the Requirement has no link, the Repository does not exist, the Repository is retired, the Execution is not owned by the calling Runner, or the fencing token is stale. Assert all five.

A18. The adapter re-reads the target before its first write. Immediately before the first forge call the adapter re-reads the publication target through the application layer and refuses if it disagrees with the payload it was handed on any of repository identifier, owner, name or base commit. State the reason at the call site: docs/architecture/domain-model.md section 10 requires that the next Runner not trust the Work Packet and re-observe external state, and this is the one packet that would otherwise be trusted blindly. Assert the refusal with a payload that disagrees, and assert that no process was started.

A19. Branch namespace, measured. Every published ref is refs/heads/agentic-loop/<increment_id>/<execution_id>, computed by one pure function that is the only producer of a ref name, so retrying one operation targets one ref and a second Execution gets its own. Assert the ref name is a deterministic function of those two identifiers and that a name outside the reserved prefix is refused. Record in the runner evidence the measured fact that this repository's only two push-triggered workflows filter branches v2 and main respectively, with the file and the trigger block named, so the reserved prefix triggers neither.

A20. The whole protocol runs through the real dispatcher with only the transport injected. One test constructs the real OutboxDispatcher over the real memory store with the real sink and the real observer, and injects the transport as a function, not as a process and not as a fake dispatcher or a fake store. It must cover, as separate cases: created and confirmed; already present and convergent; present and disagreeing, reaching needs-input; and an unknown outcome reaching ambiguous, then read-after-write, then confirmed in one case and needs-input in another. Assert that the operation identifier equals the idempotency key on every attempt, that a stale fence yields superseded with no transport call at all, and that a control intent denying external effects for the repository scope prevents delivery.

A21. Non_goal 2, three ways. (i) An AST control asserts that internal/application/publication.go, internal/runner/forgepublish.go and internal/runner/publishsource.go contain no call that saves a Requirement or an Increment. (ii) A behavioural test asserts that after a confirmed publication the Requirement's status and version are unchanged from before the publication, and that no requirement event was recorded. (iii) The Observation's vocabulary carries no completed value, per A14. Additionally, contracts/release-contract/** must be byte-identical and cap-autonomous-resolution must not be claimed, weakened, narrowed or reinterpreted; report git diff --stat for contracts/ to prove it.

A22. Write-once per operation identifier, in both stores. Writing the identical Observation for the same operation identifier again is an idempotent replay and not a second record; writing a different Observation for the same operation identifier is a conflict refusal. The bounded per-increment read applies its bound in the storage query, as a single-field equality query bounded in the shape internal/store/firestore/store.go already uses, so no composite index is needed: firestore.indexes.json must be byte-identical and git diff --stat must prove it. Both store implementations must satisfy the same tests.

A23. make check reaches no network and starts no gh child. No test inside make check may resolve a hostname, open a socket or start the forge CLI. The origin in every make check test is a bare repository created at test time by the real git binary in t.TempDir(); commit no git fixture, pack file or bare directory. Record the measured fact that the forge CLI is absent from the validated pure PATH while git and unshare are present, so a bare exec by name would work on the host and fail in the validated environment, which is why absolute path resolution is required rather than defensive.

A24. The single live leg, gated, owner-designated, and never defaulted. One test gated on a forge-write gate variable set to 1 together with an owner-supplied <owner>/<name> designation. With the gate set and the designation absent it FAILS naming the missing designation; with the gate unset it skips and the skip is recorded with status skipped and its reason, never as a pass. There must be no hardcoded default and in particular no default to the Loop's own registered repository. The leg must: log the execution environment identifiers (machine and kernel from uname -srm, go version, the resolved absolute git path with its version, the resolved absolute forge CLI path with its version, and the designated repository); assert before the write that no push argv is constructible; produce a real commit through the real git adapter inside the real namespace; publish through the real dispatcher; measure all four equalities of A9 against the real forge; measure the workflow-run count for the branch and require zero; record the ref, the published commit, the published tree and observed_at; and print the exact owner-run command that deletes the ref. Do not delete the ref: the branch is the artefact a person reads.

A25. G6b, measured and not argued. Publish .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-072-live-exercise-files.json following .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-075-live-exercise-files.json exactly: the same reproduction argv for recomputing the compiled set, with the exercising package and test name of this task's live leg substituted, plus the observation commit, observed_at, the path count and any out-of-tree executable with its resolved path and version. The live record must carry its observation commit so the observation-to-judgement intersection can be recomputed. Do not edit V2-075's artifact.

A26. Live task completion rule. After the component keys and the G6b file set are measured, do not edit any file that the live exercise compiles. If a later fix requires such an edit, re-run the live leg and re-measure both, and say so in the record; do not argue that the edit was harmless.

A27. Evidence, eight records, keys read from the final green tree. Write one record per component this task exercises -- domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, runner, docs -- plus one live record under the component name forge-live-write, register each in .agents/v2/evidence/index.json with task_id V2-072 as the producer, and make the ledger tests in internal/contracts green as the definition of done. The api record exists because the api component key moves through its declared runner dependency while internal/api/** is a prohibited path and unchanged: its checks are the re-run of that component's own check target and the recorded key, and its summary must say exactly that. The live record's evidence_key is a synthetic key: state the computation in the record itself as the sha256 of the concatenated constituent component keys, name the constituents, and show the value so a gate can recompute it. Do not use a component name beginning with provider-live- or gcp-live-, which would demand a preflight record this task has none of.

A28. The measured moved-key table. Capture make evidence-keys before the change and again on the final green tree, and record in the runner evidence a table of every component whose key moved, with the component name, the earlier key and the final key. Every evidence record this task writes must carry the final green tree's key for its own component. For a component whose key moved but for which this task writes no record, record the movement in that table and state that G6a carries its freshness because make check re-runs its checks; do not edit another task's evidence record. The measured expectation from the manifest is that runner is a declared dependency of api, store-firestore and control-plane and that domain is a dependency of application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, reconciler, release, runner, scheduler and control-plane, so the table is expected to be larger than the record set; report the actual measurement, not this expectation.

A29. Read the keys after committing the evidence, then confirm the tree. Read each component key from make evidence-keys on the final green tree after removing build/evidence and after committing the evidence, then confirm make check is green on that commit. Before that commit, run the repository's secret scan over the ledger directory only, with the repository configuration, and report its verdict.

A30. Determinism is acceptance, not preference. No fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test. Every wait is bounded deadline polling against an injected clock, and a measured duration is logged as an observation, never asserted as a threshold. The forge child's lifetime is bounded by a context deadline, not by a timer.

A31. Counts, verdicts and skips. Report the before and after top-level test count per touched package: internal/domain, internal/application, internal/store/memory, internal/store/firestore, internal/runner. Measure the baseline yourself on the starting tree rather than trusting a quoted number, and report both numbers. Every pre-existing test must keep passing under its existing name with its assertions unchanged. Judge every devbox run by its verdict line, not by devbox run's exit code, which is unreliable in this environment. A skipped test is never counted as a pass.

A32. Documentation of record. Write docs/operations/forge-publication.md covering: the reserved branch prefix and the ref naming rule; the four content-addressed equalities; the create-only and never-forced rule; the three outcomes and where needs-input goes; the owner-run command that deletes a published ref; the two residues that deletion does NOT remove, namely the objects reachable by object name and the repository's own activity entry; the gate variables and the fact that the target is owner-designated with no default; and the statement that no production loop calls Dispatch yet. Do not edit any other document.
constraints: Work only inside the assigned isolated task worktree; never push. Never use git reset, git checkout --, git stash or git commit --amend.

Do not touch ci/components.json, ci/**, Makefile, go.mod, go.sum or devbox.*. V2-045's manifest surface check (internal/ci TestManifestDependencySurface, TestDerivedGraphMatchesDeclaredNarrowings) will turn make check red if a new import edge is undeclared: if that happens, STOP and escalate to the tech_lead. Do not edit the manifest to make it pass. Note that internal/runner already imports internal/application, so the sink needs no new edge; if you find yourself wanting a new package, that is the signal to stop.
Do not touch .agents/v2/task-state/** or any .agents/v2/packets/** file; the coordinator records transitions and packets.

internal/domain/model.go, control.go, lease.go, release.go and id.go are untouchable, and so are contracts/release-contract/** and contracts/schemas/**. No capability declaration may be weakened, narrowed or reinterpreted to match the result, and cap-autonomous-resolution must not be claimed: Preview observation and Stable reflection still depend on a Preview deploy that does not exist.

internal/runner/git.go, sourcecontrol.go, forge.go, confinement.go, supervisor.go, workspace.go, secret_guard.go, secret_broker.go and source_guard_test.go are untouchable. The new work reuses them as they are and must leave git diff --stat empty for every one of them.

No git push, ever, and no argv naming push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential or worktree. Do not add an entry to the git subcommand allowlist or to the two-key -c option allowlist. Do not run gh auth setup-git, gh auth token or gh auth git-credential, and do not write credential.helper at repository, global or system scope. Do not allowlist HOME into the git child's environment.

Do not relax NamespaceConfinement, do not add a namespace option, and do not run any git child unconfined except the one that was already unconfined because it writes nothing. If the namespace Probe fails in this environment, STOP and escalate with the recorded kernel identifier and Probe's reason; do not skip and count it as a pass.

No credential value may enter argv, the environment, a file, a log, a record, a document or an evidence summary, in any form. The forge CLI reads its own store; the granted set is empty; request bodies travel on standard input.
No raw forge response, no child standard error and no HTTP status text may be recorded, returned, logged or journaled. Standard error is discarded and standard output is bounded by a hard byte cap.
make check must reach no network and must start no forge CLI child. No test inside make check may resolve a hostname or open a socket, and no git fixture may be committed.

The live target is owner-designated with no default and never the Loop's own registered repository by default. If the owner designates nothing, STOP: set nothing, fabricate nothing, and escalate so the coordinator can record blocked with block_reason beginning external-unavailable: and next_owner sol. A local, emulated or faked result may never be registered as satisfying a condition that names the real forge (G3.1).

Never force a ref, never update a ref, never delete a ref from code, and never construct a body containing a key named force. The live leg must not delete the branch it published: the branch is the artefact.

Never fake git, the namespace, the forge CLI or a signal in any gate-bearing test (docs/architecture/validation.md). Only the in-process transport of the deterministic protocol test may be injected, and it must be a function rather than a fake dispatcher or a fake store.
Determinism is acceptance, not preference: no fixed sleep, no wall-clock timer and no goroutine in any new test. Waiting is bounded deadline polling with an injected clock.

A skipped test is never counted as a pass (gate rule G7). Record every skip explicitly with status skipped and its reason. Record the execution environment identifier in every evidence record: machine and kernel from uname -srm, go version, devbox environment, the resolved absolute git path with its version, and, in the live record, the resolved absolute forge CLI path with its version and the identifier of the real repository written to.

Do not edit .agents/v2/evidence/artifacts/V2-075-live-exercise-files.json or any evidence record produced by another task. Reuse V2-075's published argv for the file-set computation; do not invent a second method.

Do not add an HTTP endpoint, an OpenAPI field, a read model, a view or an owner console block in this task. internal/api/**, internal/web/**, contracts/openapi/** and internal/application/readmodels.go are prohibited paths, and the human-readable pointer for this task is the branch on the forge plus the recorded Observation.
Do not wire a long-running dispatcher into cmd/**. cmd/** is a prohibited path and the scheduled dispatcher is a separate, named follow-on.

Do not create a Pull Request, a release, a tag, an issue, a comment or any other forge object beyond the blob, tree, commit and single branch ref this task publishes. Do not start a real Provider CLI (codex, claude, opencode) and do not touch any Google Cloud resource.

Commit no git fixture and leave no probe ref: the repository's secret scan reads every ref, so a commit created by a test must live only in a temporary repository outside this working tree. Before finishing, run git for-each-ref in the task worktree and report that it names no probe or working-copy ref.

When writing a digest into prose, match the .gitleaks.toml allowlist form: a bare 64-hex or 40-hex value followed by at most one punctuation character, and never an identifier adjacent to it. Prefer naming the kind of digest over quoting its value.
Run the repository's secret scan over the ledger directory only, with the repository configuration, before committing evidence; do not scan the repository root, which picks up build output.

Never write a verification as passed that was not actually executed. If an acceptance item cannot be satisfied, STOP and escalate to the tech_lead rather than fabricating, weakening or reinterpreting it.

Escalate rather than proceed if: make check goes red on the manifest surface check; any existing test in internal/application/outbox_test.go requires a change; the forge refuses a request body this design predicts will be accepted, naming the refused step; the namespace Probe fails; a top-level test count decreases in any touched package; the owner designates no live target; or the live read-after-write finds a ref that already exists and disagrees, which is a needs-input outcome in production but a stop condition for this task's own live leg.

Rollback has two halves and both must be written down. Source: reverting the commits on the task branch and deleting the branch restores the tree completely, because both new records are additive and empty for every pre-existing Requirement and Increment, the single outbox.go addition is one unused sentinel once removed, and no existing record's shape changes. External: the published ref is NOT rolled back by any source revert -- it is removed only by the explicit owner-run ref delete recorded in the live evidence and in docs/operations/forge-publication.md, and two residues survive even that, namely the created objects which stay reachable by object name and the repository's own activity entry which cannot be deleted at all. Never claim the external effect is fully reversible.
Judge every devbox run by its verdict line (make check's own final verdict, 'E2E group passed', 'Lint passed'), not by the exit code of devbox run, which is unreliable in this environment.
